key_insight: This paper proposes a new way to evaluate AI agents on open-ended AI research, moving beyond narrow benchmarks and noisy peer review. Early case studies suggest this approach can better reveal whether agents are making real progress toward automating AI R&D.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations of AI agents miss the core challenge of AI research: open-ended work with ambiguous goals, iterative decisions, and no single correct answer. The paper addresses the lack of reliable evidence on whether agents can actually conduct meaningful AI research.
method: Introduces a third evaluation framework for measuring progress toward AI R&D automation.
Uses AI agents to tackle central, open-ended research tasks rather than only narrow, verifiable ones.
Tests the approach through two early case studies to gather evidence on agent research capability.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more realistic way to assess research-capable agents and identify where they still fail. It can help guide the design, benchmarking, and deployment of systems aimed at automating parts of the research process.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of three evaluation styles: narrow benchmarks, blind peer review, and the new open-ended research evaluation
Workflow diagram showing an AI agent performing an end-to-end research task
Case study summary cards with task, outcome, and key limitation
Progress meter or ladder illustrating the path from task completion to AI R&D automation
paper_title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
paper_authors: Peter Kirgis, Sayash Kapoor, Andrew Schwartz, Stephan Rabanser, David Africa
